data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"RFC 9110 distinguishes safe from idempotent by side-effect permission: a safe method is intended only for retrieval and has no intended action beyond retrieval (section 9.2.1), while an idempotent method may have side effects but multiple identical requests have the same intended effect as one (section 9.2.2). An append-only log writer cannot be safe because appending changes durable state; it must be idempotent so that at-least-once redelivery of the same event yields the same log state as a single append.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If duplicate appends are allowed to create distinct log entries and downstream replay is sensitive to multiplicity, this idempotent-writer claim fails.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the transport already guarantees exactly-once delivery, idempotence is not exercised though it may still be defensive.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the relevant protocol defines idempotence by identical responses rather than identical resulting server state, a retry returning 'already exists' instead of 'created' could violate the claim.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Key the event by a stable content/idempotency identifier and make the write a conditional append or upsert: if the identifier already exists, return without adding a new entry; if not, append exactly once. Thus the state transition for duplicate retries is S -> S union {e} after first and S -> S on later duplicates, equal to the single successful write.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
